Nilgiris Fishing Rules, 1966
Published vide Notification No. G. O. Ms. No. 1442, Agriculture, dated 26th April 1966 S.R.O. No. A-420 of 1966
G. O. Ms. No. 1442, Agriculture, dated 26th April 1966, S.R.O. No. A-420 of 1966. - In exercise of the powers conferred
by sections 4 and 5 of the Nilgiris Game and Fish Preservation Act, 1875 (Tamil Nadu Act II of 1879); sections 26,33
and 63 of the Tamil Nadu Forest Act, 1882 (Tamil Nadu Act V of 1882), and section 6 of the Indian Fisheries Act, 1897
(Central Act IV of 1897) and in supersession of the Nilgiris Fishing Rules published with the late Development
Department Notification No. Nil, dated 23rd October 1953, published at pages 378-381 of Rules Supplement to Part I of
the Fort St. George Gazette, dated 18th November, 1953, as subsequently amended, the Governor of Tamil Nadu
hereby makes the following rules the same having been previously published for general information:-

1.
Short title, application and direction.
Page 1/14
 
Nilgiris Fishing Rules, 1966
(a)
These rules may be called the Nilgiris Fishing Rules, 1966.
(b)
They shall apply to the waters within the area specified in Schedule I to these rules;
(c)
These rules shall remain in force for a period of fifteen to twenty seven years from the date of the publication in the
Official Gazette.

2.
Definitions.
- In these rules, unless the context otherwise requires,-
(a)
"Assistant Director" means the Assistant Director of Fisheries having jurisdiction over the Nilgiris District;
(b)
"Director" means the Director of Fisheries, [Chennai]
[Substituted for the word 'Madras' by the City of Madras (Alteration of Name) Act, 1996 (Tamil Nadu Act 28 of 1996).]
;
(c)
"Fishing" means and includes capture of, or attempt to capture, fish by any means including hooks and lines, fixed
engines, curves, weirs or nets or by damming or baling of any water;
(d)
"Government" means the Government of Tamil Nadu;
(e)
"Inspector" means the Inspector of Fisheries.

3.
Waters in which fishing is controlled by the Department of Fisheries.
- The Fisheries Department shall control fishing in all the waters specified in Schedules II to IV to these rules.

4.
Prohibition of erection or use of fixed engines, etc., and fishing.
- No person shall-
(a)
erect or use any fixed engine or net for capturing fish;
(b)
use any poison or throw any toxic matter likely to result in fish mortality;
(c)
use dynamite or other explosive substance for fishing;
(d)
fish in any other method in the waters within the area specified in Schedule I to these rules except under, and in
accordance with, the terms and conditions of a licence issued in the Form set out in Schedule V to these rules.

5.
Authority to issue licences and the period.
(1)
Fishing licences shall be issued by any officer of the Fisheries Department not below the rank of an Assistant Inspector
of Fisheries or any other person, or association authorised in this behalf by the Director.
(2)
The period covered by a licence shall be clearly endorsed on the licence.

7.
Cancellation or refusal.
- The Officer issuing the licence may cancel the licence or refuse to issue a further licence to any person who fails to
Page 2/14
 
Nilgiris Fishing Rules, 1966
comply with the provisions of these rules.

8.
Fees not to be refunded.
- No refund of the licence fees paid shall be made on any category of licence, (whether used or unused or cancelled),
unless the licence is surrendered at least two clear days in advance of the date of commencement of the licence.

9.
Furnishing of information by persons holding monthly and annual licences.
- Every holder of a monthly or annual licence shall send a report in the Form specified in Schedule VI to these rules
within seven days of the close of each calendar month during the period of validity of the licence.

10.
Time for fishing.
- No licensee shall fish before 6 a.m. and after 7 p.m.

11.
Rules for trout fishing.
(a)
Trout fishing shall be allowed in all the waters specified in Schedule II to these rules.
(b)
Fishing in the waters specially reserved for trout fishing, and in the tributaries of such waters shall be, subject to the
following provisions, namely:-
(i)
The holder of a trout fishing licence may also take any other fish he may catch in the said waters. He may also fish in the
waters mentioned in Schedule 111 to these rules, subject to the rules regulating fishing in these waters, but without
alterations of the maximum catch of trout allowed on his trout licence, the holder of an annual licence for mixed fishing
may, on payment of an additional sum of Rs. 50 (Rupees fifty only) per year or such other sum as may be fixed, from
time to time, by the Director, obtain a yearly licence for trout fishing.
(ii)
Fishing shall be closed in these waters including tributaries of such waters during such periods-as may, from time to
time, be notified by the Director in the Nilgiris and Coimbatore District Gazette.
(iii)
Fishing in the waters specially reserved for trout fishing or in the tributaries of such waters shall be with artificial fly or
flies on a single hook only. No weight in any form shall be attached to the cast, fly or line. Spinning may be permitted in
such water or waters by the Director in writing.
(iv)
For the purpose of this rules, "spinning" means the use of artificial minnows, lure or spoon and dead bait (which means
dead fish only) used with spinner or by attaching to the hook or hooks a dead fish so placed (i.e. by arranging the tail) as
to spin in the water. The use of live bait is strictly prohibited. On no account shall unrequired bail dead or alive, be
thrown into the lakes.
(v)
Trolling in the Kukurti, Emerald, Avalanche and Upper Bhavani Reservoirs, within the limits specified on the notice
boards in the office of the Assistant Director or Inspector, is permitted during such period as spinning is permitted.
(vi)
All fishes of a length less than that fixed, from time to time, by the Director should be returned alive to the waters where
they have been captured.
(vii)
Every licence holder should carry a disgorger.
(viii)
All trout bearing marks by the Fisheries Department of the Government for experimental purposes should, after capture,
be surrendered intact to the nearest Fisheries Officer with information regarding the place, date and time of capture.

12.

13.
Issue of more than one licence.
(1)
No person shall take more than three annual licences in a year for fishing in any of the waters.
(2)
The Director may vary the maximum number and size of trout which can be captured with a trout licence of any
description in such manner and for such period as he thinks fit.

14.
Rules for mixed fishing (trout and carps).
(1)
Fishing any species of fish with one rod and a single or triple hook bait or lure shall be permitted in the waters mentioned
in Schedule III to these rules which are not reserved for trout fishing, but in which trout may also be available.
(2)
The fees for such licences and the number of trouts which a licensee is entitled to catch shall be as specified in the table

15.
Rules for carp fishing.
(1)
Carp fishing shall be allowed in the waters mentioned in Schedule IV to these rules.
(2)
The following fees shall be charged for licences for fishing in such waters with one rod and any bait lure or hook (except
in the case of masheer for which triple hook is permitted).
(i)
Daily-Rs. 3 (Rupees Three only).
(ii)
Monthly-(30 days from the date of issue) - Rs. 30 (Rupees Thirty only).
(iii)
Annual (12 months from the date of issue)-Rs. 75 (Rupees Seventy-five only).

16.
General conditions of licence for trout, mixed and carp fishing.
(1)
Licences issued are not transferable and shall be shown on demand to any Fisheries, Forest, Revenue or Police Officer
or any person authorised by the Director.
(2)
Licence holders shall, on demand, show their catches to any or all of the above officers or persons.

17.
Cancellation or refusal of licence for conviction or other reasons.
- The officer issuing licences may refuse to grant a licence under these rules to any applicant who has been convicted of
an offence against the provision of these rules or for any other reason to be stated in writing and may, on, similar
grounds, cancel any licence already granted. When a licence is so cancelled, the fees paid for the licence shall not be
refunded.

18.
No refund of fee if declared to be closed for fishing.
- If during the currency of any category of licence, any water or waters or portions of waters thereof either specially
reserved for trout fishing or otherwise are declared as closed for fishing for any reason or purpose whatsoever, the
holder of a licence for fishing in such waters shall have no claim of refund of the licence fee or any portion thereof in
respect of the licence held by him.

19.
Prohibition of the use of more than one rod.
- The use of more than one rod at a time under one licence is prohibited. For the purposes of this rule, a rod which is not
in the licence holder's hand, but which is left with its line in the water shall be considered to be a rod in use.

20.
Powers of the Director.
(1)
Page 5/14
 
Nilgiris Fishing Rules, 1966
The Director may, by notification in the Nilgiris and Coimbatore District Gazette,-
(i)
declare, from time to time, that all or any of the waters whether reserved for trout fishing or not are closed or open to
fishing; or
(ii)
prohibit the fishing of any particular species of fish in all or any or portions of any or all waters for any specified period.
(2)
Notwithstanding anything contained in these rules, the Director may, by notification in the Gazettes of Nilgiris and
Coimbatore districts,-
(i)
reduce or increase the rate of fee for a trout or mixed or carp fishing licence;
(ii)
decide the method of catching trout or other species of fishes;
(iii)
permit spinning or other methods of fishing in any of the waters reserved for trout fishing;
(iv)
declare any trout water as mixed fishing water and any mixed fishing waters as trout fishing water;
(v)
permit or disallow the use of power boats or other kind of boats in any of the waters, subject to general or special
concurrence of the Tamil Nadu State Electricity Board or any officer authorised by the Board for giving such
concurrence;
(vi)
permit any method considered necessary to eradicate undesirable fish in any of the waters;
(vii)
permit the use of fixed engines in any or all waters for the purpose of fishing;
(viii)
fix hours for fishing;
(ix)
approve the forms of fishing licences;
(xi)
authorise any person or body or group of persons other than the Fisheries Officers to issue any or all licences for fishing
and prescribe the procedure and conditions for issue of licences by such persons or organisation.

21.
Penalties.
(1)
Whoever commits a breach of the rules hereinbefore contained shall be punishable with fine which may extend to one
hundred rupees and when the breach is a continuing breach with a further fine, which may extend to ten rupees for
every day after the date of the first conviction during which the breach is proved to have been persisted in.
(2)
A Magistrate may, on the conviction of any person for the breach of these rules, order the seizure, forfeiture and removal
of fixed engines erected or used or nets used in contravention of these rules and also order the forfeiture of any fish
taken by means of any such fixed engine or net.
(3)
Whoever commits breach of rules, 4,11,12,14,15 and 16 shall be punishable with imprisonment for a term which may
extend to one month or with fine which may extend to two hundred rupees or with both.

22.
Persons appointed to enforce these rules to be deemed to be Forest Officers.
- Every person appointed or authorised by, or acting under the orders of the Director for the purpose of enforcing these
rules shall be deemed to be a Forest Officer under the Tamil Nadu Forest Act, 1882 (Tamil Nadu Act V of 1882).

23.
Savings.

5. Fishing shall not be permitted between 19.30 hours and 06.00 hours excepting Mukurthi lake where fishing is
permitted till 21.00 hours.
(a)
Spinning is permitted with the permission of the Director of Fisheries in the Mukurthi and Upper Bhavani lakes and in the
Avalanche and Emerald lakes only in those areas demarcated by notice Board.
Spinning is defined as the use of:-
Artificial minnow lure or spoon and (ii) dead bait (which means fish only) used with a spinner or by attaching to the hook
or hooks a dead fish so placed, (e.g. by arranging tail) as to spin in the waters. The use of live and unrequired baits are
strictly prohibited.
In case of fishing waters any bait or line may be used.

6. Fishing at any time with more than one rod is prohibited (a rod with the line and hook left in the water shall be
considered to be a rod and line in use even though it is not held in the Angler's hand).
7. All fish of length less than that fixed, from time to time, by the Director must be returned alive to the waters.

9. The following fees are charged for a licence for one rod and line per angler:-
For one year
Rs. 75 to cover 250 trouts.
For one month (30 days from any chosen date)
Rs. 25 to cover 75 trouts.
For one week (seven days from any chosen date)
Rs. 10 to cover 25 trouts.
For one week end (Friday noon to Monday noon)
Rs. 5 to cover 15 trouts.
For one day
Rs. 3 to cover 6 trouts.
Note. - The licence ceases to be valid after the expiry of the period even if the maximum allowance of fish is not caught.

10. Every holder of licence must furnish after each month or week in respect of annual and monthly licences and within
Iwo days of the expiry of the licences for weekly, week end, daily licences the informations as to the water-fished,
number and weight of fishes caught and killed, and number returned alive to the waters and individual size and weight of
fishes of 500 grams and above for which cards can be obtained from the office of the issue of the licence.

11. The officer issuing the licence may cancel the licence or refuse to issue a licence to any person who fails to comply
with any or all the provisions of Nilgiris Fishing Rules, and no refund of licence fee paid will be made under any
circumstances.

12. The licence is not transferable and shall be shown on demand to any Police, Fisheries, Forest, or Revenue Officer.
Tire licence holder must, on demand, show the catches also to any or all the officers or persons mentioned above, or
persons authorised by them in this behalf.
Note. - The licence not being transferable, a licence holder may not lend his rod to any persons not holding licence nor
can airy such person use the rod of the licence holder.

13. No licence holder may take fish for purposes of stocking in private waters and all fish retained must be killed
immediately at the water side.

14. Licence fee once paid is not refundable or adjustable subject to rule 8.
